title: Add cache hit-rate dashboard panels + initial alert rules (conservative thresholds)
author: Sergio Costa
description: Summary: Adds first-pass dashboard panels for prefix/KV cache efficiency and supporting signals (eviction pressure + wasted prefill), and introduces conservative alert rules intended as guardrails during rollout. Motivation: With runtime instrumentation landing in the monorepo (cache hit/miss counters, eviction/pressure metrics, wasted prefill), SRE needs a standard triage surface to answer: (1) did hit-rate actually drop, (2) why, and (3) is it eviction/pressure vs config/policy vs workload mix. This PR is intentionally conservative on paging; most alerts are ticket-level until we tune against real workload patterns. What’s included (Dashboards): 1) Cache Efficiency Overview (new row): KV cache hit-rate (time series) with filters: deployment_mode, region, model_family, route_group; prefix cache reuse effectiveness (reused_tokens / prefill_tokens) as both time series and heatmap by prompt_length_bucket; cache miss reason breakdown (stacked area) using miss_reason allowlist (capacity, ttl_expired, policy_disabled, hash_mismatch, version_mismatch, unknown); wasted prefill ratio (wasted_prefill_tokens / prefill_tokens) with request-volume gating annotation. 2) Eviction & Pressure (new row): KV cache eviction rate (evictions/s) with eviction_reason breakdown where available; memory pressure gauges for KV/prefix caches (normalized 0..1) and “time in pressure” indicator; “top contributors” table by route_group and model_family for high wasted prefill (kept to aggregated dimensions to avoid cardinality blowups). What’s included (Alerts): - cache_hit_rate_drop_guardrail: fires when KV hit-rate drops below 0.35 for 30m AND req_count > 5000 in the same window; severity=ticket; includes label set limited to {deployment_mode, region, model_family}. - cache_eviction_pressure_high: fires when pressure > 0.90 for 15m with eviction_rate > 10/s; severity=ticket; intended to flag memory pressure events that correlate with latency and cache churn. - wasted_prefill_spike: fires when wasted_prefill_ratio > 0.55 for 30m AND prefill_tokens_total > 5e6; severity=ticket; this is a noisy metric early on, so threshold is intentionally high. Notes on cardinality and joinability: This PR only slices on stable/low-cardinality dimensions (deployment_mode, region, model_family, route_group) and does not include per-tenant identifiers. Route-level is represented as route_group (gateway-level grouping) until ingestion-side cardinality guards (PR #613) are fully rolled out. Dependencies / Links: - Runtime metrics: redwood PRs #18421/#18422/#18423/#18424/#18430/#18431 (naming alignment) - Sampling/rate limits: redwood PR #18425 - Context propagation: redwood PR #18426 - Cardinality guards: observability-pack PR #613 (follow-up) - Linear: ENG-4824 (dashboards/alerts), ENG-4821 (metric definitions/tags) Testing: - jsonnetfmt + dashboard compilation (CI) - promtool rule validation (CI) - Local render against staging datasource config to verify queries return series (manual) Rollout plan: - Merge behind existing folder structure; dashboards disabled by default in prod until the runtime flag is enabled. - Once runtime telemetry is on in canary, SRE will validate panels for 48h and then enable global dashboard navigation link. - Alerts remain ticket-level until Aisha/Allison tune based on diurnal patterns and workload mix; paging policy explicitly out of scope for this PR.
commits: dashboards/cache_efficiency: add KV hit-rate, prefix reuse, wasted prefill panels
dashboards/cache_efficiency: add miss reason breakdown + annotations for volume gating
alerts/cache: add guardrail rules for hit-rate drop, eviction pressure, wasted prefill spike

ci: promtool validation for new rule group
